events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Broward, FL; Miami-Dade, FL
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
counties, Broward and Miami-Dade.

* WHEN...Until 415 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or
is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 222 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause urban and small stream
flooding. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hollywood, Miramar, Hallandale, Miami Gardens, North Miami,
North Miami Beach, Dania Beach, Opa-Locka, West Park, Ojus,
Hard Rock Stadium, Golden Glades, Westview, Pembroke Park,
Ives Estates, Hollywood Downtown and Saint Thomas University.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The National Weather Service in Paducah has issued a Flood Warning
for the following river in Illinois...Indiana...

Wabash River at New Harmony.

.Heavy rainfall last week continues to cause slow rises on the Wabash
River.  At New Harmony, the river is forecast to climb above flood
stage Tuesday, and crest just under a foot above flood stage
Thursday.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at New Harmony.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning to Saturday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:30 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Tuesday morning to a crest of 15.8 feet early Thursday afternoon.
It will then fall below flood stage late Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet and dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...West-facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant southwesterly swell driven by
the monsoon pattern and Tropical Depression 19W, well north-
northwest of Yap, is producing hazardous surf and dangerous rip
currents along west-facing reefs through this afternoon.
